title: N66604-Mastery of the Seas Office Hours
description: Mastery of the Seas Industry Office Hours Announcement Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Division Newport OFFICE HOURS: The Naval Undersea Warfare Center, Division Newport (NUWCDIVNPT) will be holding Mastery of the Seas Office Hours. During these office hours, Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) from the Mastery of the Seas Capability Focus Areas and other NUWC representatives will be available to discuss the strategic vision of the Center with a specific focus on how external industry can participate and contribute to the mission. This event will be held on a recurring bi-monthly basis with an in-person and online option. title: Pre-Solicitation Notice and Pre-Solicitation Meeting/Industry Day announcement for Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-sUAS)
description: ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. It is anticipated that Foreign Allied Participation will be excluded at the prime contractor level. A technical library relating to the subject area of this acquisition will be made available. Potential Offerors will first need to request access through AFRL/RI personnel. Full instructions and contact information are contained within attachment 1 of this posting. For planning purposes, potential Offerors who wish to gain access to the Technical Read Library will be required to sign a �Statement of Terms for Receipt of Technical Read Library Access�, provide a copy of an approved DD Form 2345 �Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement�, and provide a letter from the Data Custodian designated on that form authorizing access by whomever will be reviewing the library. Evaluation of the capability packages received in response to the Request for Information (RFI-RIKD-19-01) resulted in a determination that a small business set-aside could be established. A Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for this effort is anticipated to be released during the 1st quarter of CY 2020. Potential Offerors will be encouraged to review and comment on the Draft RFP, including the Statement of Work (SOW) and Sections L and M. Please monitor this notice for updates. THE ENTIRE SOLICITATION WILL BE ISSUED ON THE BETA SAM WEBSITE AT https://beta.sam.gov/. Paper copies will not be available. title: Senior Procurement Executive Message to the Department of State Contractor and Federal Assistance Community on the Lapse in Appropriations
description: Senior Procurement Executive Message to the Department of State Contractor and Federal Assistance Community on the Lapse in Appropriations As the Department�s Senior Procurement Executive, I am reaching out to share guidance due to the lapse in appropriations that occurred on October 1, 2025. This guidance relates to the handling of Department, including US Agency for International Development (USAID), contract and federal assistance (grants) awards, that is consistent with Department and Office of Management and Budget�s Guidance on Operations During a Lapse in Appropriations. The Antideficiency Act prohibits agencies from incurring obligations that are in advance of, or that exceed, an appropriation, with certain limited exceptions. As you are aware, a fiscal year 2026 appropriation is not yet enacted. For many Department accounts, this results in a lapse in funds designated to purchase certain supplies and services and issue grants and reduces the Department�s capacity to provide oversight on contracts and grants. As a result, certain planned procurements and grants may be cancelled, or postponed, and certain existing contracts and grants may be stopped, suspended, reduced in scope, or terminated. Additionally, payments may be delayed. If the lapse directly affects a contract or grant, on or about October 1, 2025, the Department�s contracting officers and grant officers will notify contractors and recipients of the status of their contract or grant. If a contract or grant will not be affected at the onset of the lapse in appropriations, the Department does not plan to provide any separate notifications or communications of that fact. Unless the contracting officer or grants officer provides a formal notification to the contrary, all Department contractors and recipients must continue to comply with all terms, conditions, requirements and deliveries specified in their contracts or grants. Once a Continuing Resolution or full-year appropriation is signed into law, the Department will begin implementing the plan to orderly resume activity and will notify contractors/recipients at that time. Thank you for your continued partnership with the Department, and for your cooperation as we work together to manage this lapse in appropriations.

title: P309 Replace School Age Care Centers Camp Foster and Camp McTureous, Okinawa Japan
description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE W912HV26BA007 FY26 MCN P309, School Age Care Centers Replacement Camp Foster and McTureous, Okinawa, Japan The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Japan District (POJ) is providing a PRE-SOLICITATION notice pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 5.101(a) (https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul) for an upcoming Invitation for Bid (IFB). title: Cyber Platform
description: NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk, Contracting Department, Pentagon Directorate intends to acquire, via small business set aside, a commercial cybersecurity training and certification platform for National Defense University (NDU), College of Information and Cyberspace (CIC). NDU CIC has a requirement to procure a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS), web-based cybersecurity training and certification platform to support the educational, cyber workforce development, and operational readiness mission of the National Defense University (NDU), College of Information and Cyberspace (CIC) (NDU-CIC). The Government seeks a commercially available Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) cybersecurity training platform that provides immersive, hands-on cyber learning, realistic cyber laboratory environments, structured learning pathways, cyber range exercises, and cybersecurity certification preparation capabilities that enhance cyber workforce readiness, operational problem-solving, critical thinking, and cyber mission effectiveness. The platform shall support Joint Professional Military Education (JPME), Department of Defense (DoD) cyber workforce development initiatives, cyber upskilling, and cyber readiness activities for authorized faculty, staff, and students through Internet-based access to interactive cybersecurity exercises, practical laboratories, and modular cybersecurity training content. This procurement is anticipated to be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP) purchase order. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code is 611420 �Computer Training� and the Small Business Size Standard is $16 million in annual receipts. The FSC Code is DH10. It is the intent of the Government to process this procurement under FAR 12, Acquisition of Commercial Products and Services, and to award a single purchase order. Quoters will be required to submit a quote in response to the forthcoming Request for Quote (RFQ). The Government anticipates that the resultant purchase order will be awarded on a best value basis where the technical will be more considered more important than the price. Upon its release, the solicitation will be issued electronically and be available for downloading at the SAM website: https://sam.gov/content/home. It is anticipated that the RFQ will be issued no earlier than 26 August 2026. The closing date for the receipt of offers will be set forth in the RFQ Paper copies, faxed copies, or email copies of the solicitation will not be provided. Interested parties are solely responsible for monitoring the above website for posting of the RFQ and any amendments thereto. The Government will not pay for the information received. All responsible sources may submit a quote, which will be considered by NAVSUP Fleet Logistics Center Norfolk, Contracting Department, Pentagon Directorate. By submitting a quote , the quoter is self-certifying that neither the requestor nor the principal corporate officials and owners are currently suspended, debarred, or otherwise ineligible to receive contracts from any federal agency. Failure to do so may represent grounds for refusing to accept the offer. By submission of an offer, the contractor acknowledges the requirements that a prospective awardee must be registered in the System for Award Management (SAM) database prior to award. Lack of registration in the SAM database will make a contractor ineligible for award. Contractors may obtain information on registration and annual confirmation requirements via the internet at https://www.sam.gov/SAM/. Further, offerors are required to go on-line to the SAM website to complete their Online Representations and Certifications Application (ORCA) prior to the submittal of their proposal.

title: Responses to Vendor Questions � RFQ 19NL8026Q0007 MSG Cook Services, The Hague, The Netherlands
description: "SEE ATTACHED" Responses to Vendor Questions � RFQ 19NL8026Q0007 MSG Cook Services, The Hague, The Netherlands Notice: Close of Question Period Issued: August 10, 2026 at 12:45 hours (local time) The Government thanks all prospective Offerors for their thoughtful questions regarding RFQ 19NL8026Q0007, MSG Cook Services, The Hague, The Netherlands. The responses below represent the Government's final answers to all questions received to date. Please be advised that the question period for this solicitation is now closed, and no further questions will be accepted. Offerors should rely on the solicitation package, as clarified by this Q&A document, in preparing their final quotations. Quotations remain due by August 20, 2026, at 1700 hours (local time), submitted electronically to TheHagueContracts@state.gov in accordance with the instructions in the solicitation letter and Section 3. The Government appreciates the diligence shown by all prospective Offerors in preparing thorough, well-informed submissions. Page references to the solicitation package (RFQ 19NL8026Q0007) are provided beneath each response for traceability. Question 1 � Availability of Kitchen Photographs, Floor Plan, and Government-Furnished Property Inventory (Rephrased from: "Would the Government kindly provide photographs, a floor plan or dimensions of the MSGR kitchen and dining areas...") The Government is unable to provide photographs, floor plans, or dimensions of the MSGR kitchen and dining areas due to security concerns associated with the Marine Security Guard Residence (MSGR). The pre-quotation site visit scheduled for August 5, 2026, per Provision 52.237-1 (Site Visit), did not take place, as no prospective Offerors expressed interest in attending. Offerors must rely on the written description provided in the solicitation, including the Government Furnished Property/Equipment inventory at Attachment 2 ("all cooking pots, pans, and kitchen utensils and equipment as per attached"), together with the Performance Work Statement, to assess equipment adequacy for proposal purposes. Solicitation citations: Attachment 2 (Government Furnished Property), page 28; Section 3, Provision 52.237-1 (Site Visit), page 47. Question 2 � Minimum Staffing Requirements for the MSG Detachment Cook Position (Rephrased from: "Does the Government anticipate service being delivered by a single on-site cook...or is additional support staff...expected or permitted...") The Performance Work Statement identifies the MSG Detachment Cook as the sole Key Personnel position (Section 4.5.1). The Contractor is responsible for furnishing "all managerial, administrative, and direct labor personnel that are necessary to accomplish the work" under the contract (Section 1.0, Scope of Work). The Government does not mandate a specific staffing structure; Offerors may propose additional support staff (e.g., a kitchen helper) as needed to fully meet the requirements within their firm-fixed monthly price. Solicitation citations: Section 1.0 (Scope of Work), page 8; Section 4.5.1 (Key Personnel � Position and Function), page 11. Question 3 � Anticipated TDY Headcount Beyond the Standing Detachment (Rephrased from: "Beyond the standing detachment of up to eight (8) Marines, what are the typical and maximum numbers of TDY personnel...") Section 3.0 (Locations for Food Services) confirms the Contractor shall provide food services for up to eight (8) MSG personnel and shall accommodate additional Temporary Duty (TDY) personnel at no additional cost to the Government. For planning purposes, Offerors should anticipate a not-to-exceed range of up to four (4) additional TDY personnel during surge periods, beyond the standing eight-person detachment. Because this solicitation is for food preparation services only � and not the procurement of ingredients or supplies, which remains a separate Government-managed process under Section 1 (Prices) � any increase in MSG personnel supported during TDY periods, up to this maximum, will not result in additional cost to the Contractor. Offerors should build sufficient flexibility into portioning and menu planning to accommodate periodic increases above the standing detachment. Solicitation citations: Section 3.0 (Locations for Food Services), page 9; Section 1 (Prices), page 5. description: Notice of Sole Source Intent The Department of Interior (DOI), at the National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) intends to award a purchase order to upgrade controller and engine firmware, replace out of date network control engines, upgrade server software, and perform device and user interface programming to increase the connectivity of HVAC equipment on campus. Also provide one additional year of quarter visits to optimize system operation. The work shall be seamlessly compatible with the existing campus-wide Johnson Controls (JCI) Metasys Building Automation System (BAS). The site is at the NIFC campus at 3833 S Development Ave Boise, ID 83705. DOI has found that Johnson Controls, Inc. to be the only reasonably available source with full authority to successfully complete the required services. Since DOI�s initial market research indicates and in accordance with FAR 6.302-1 that only one responsible source can fully provide the services that will satisfy the Agency�s requirements, a Determination to Solicit from a Single Source justification is being prepared. The Government anticipates award on or before September 25, 2026 with services to begin immediately upon award to ensure the HVAC BAS is updated to alleviate disruption of services. Vendors that have questions regarding the sole source nature of the requirement or vendors that believe they can fully provide the required services are encouraged to identify themselves and give written notification to the Contracting Officer no later than September 7, 2026. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement in with convincing evidence they can furnish the requested service, and if possible, a brief price breakout of services for comparison to an Independent Government Estimate (IGE). Vendors should also describe their full authority to access Johnson Controls Metasys control server-based system since this will be a requirement during performance. All responses received will be used for market research purposes and evaluated if capable of providing the subject service. All responses should include the vendor�s Unique Entity Identifier Number and Tax Identification Number (TIN). Vendors should additionally identify themselves as either a small business or any other than small business under North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code 334512. The applicable Small Business Size Standard is 650 Emp. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based on the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will be considered solely for the market research purposes of determining whether or not to conduct a competitive procurement. EAGLE ISLAND CELL 2 IMPROVEMENTS
description: W912PM26BA008 The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Wilmington District requires a contract to perform work of the Eagle Island Cell 2 disposal area. The project includes work at Cell 2 of the Government owned Eagle Island Confined Disposal Facility (CDF) also referred to as the Dredged Material Disposal Area. The work to improve Cell 2 consists of: using existing coffer berms around spillways 4 and 5, as well as the interior of Cell 2 as borrow, raise approximately 2,000 linear feet of the low spots on the west portion of Cell 2 to EL. 46 feet NAVD88 where crest heights range from approximately EL. 37 feet NAVD88 to EL. 45 feet NAVD88 and corresponds with approximate Stations 190+00 to 210+00; raising a few bents of the timber cribbing structures associated with the outfall pipe for spillway 4; repairs to straighten spillways 4 and 5 will consist of deconstructing the riser structures, removing the footing, removing the catwalk, re-grading the bump-out to a 3H:1V slope, prepping the subgrade, pouring a 16-inch footing and reconstructing the riser structure. This solicitation is a Total Small Business Set Aside. The contract issued will be Firm Fixed Price. The Magnitude of Construction of this project is between $5,000,000.00 and $10,000,000.00. This solicitation will be issued in electronic format only and will be available on or about 12 August 2026. The bid opening date will be specified in the solicitation when it is issued. No additional media (CD-ROM, floppy disks, facsimiles, etc.) will be provided. Paper copies of this solicitation will not be available. Other methods of requesting a package will not be honored. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990 � Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction and the size standard is $45,000,000.00. Call 1-866-606-8220 for more information or visit the SAM website at www.sam.gov. After completing SAM, in order to download documents contractors and their subcontractors must register at www.sam.gov. In order to locate solicitation, Contractors can go to www. sam.gov and search for the solicitation number. Contractors can register to be put on a plan holders list that others can access through the www.sam.gov website. It is the Offeror's responsibility to check the Internet address provided as necessary for any posted changes to this solicitation and all amendments. For additional information or assistance, please contact Jenifer M. Garland, Contract Officer, email jenifer.m.garland@usace.army.mil or Diana D Curl, Contract Specialist, email diana.d.curl@usace.army.mil.

title: Pre-Solicitation Notice and Pre-Solicitation Meeting/Industry Day announcement for Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-sUAS)
description: **** Update as of 08 OCT 2020, the Tech Read Library Instructions have been updated to allow for a digital copy for review by potential Small Business Offerors. Please see below the attached updated instructions to obtain access to the Tech Read Library. The name of the document is C-sUAS Digital Tech Read Library_Instr_20201006. **** **** Update as of 28 AUG 2020, the Government's Acquisition Strategy has been approved and it has been determined that this effort will be solicited as a Small Business set-aside under NAICS 541715 Aircraft, Aircraft Engine and Engine Parts exception with size standard of 1,500 employees. Please continue to watch this posting for updates until the solicitation is released. **** ****Updated 27 AUG 2020, Posted Corrected Version of Industry Day Q&A Responses.**** ****Updated 24 AUG 2020, Posted Industry Day Q&A Responses.**** ****Updated 18 MAR 2020, Due to the COVID-19 spread and site closure the Technical Read Library Access is currently suspended until at least 11 MAY 2020. Please note that depending on the state of things this date can be pushed out further or rescined earlier.**** ****Updated 13 FEB 2020, Posted an Updated version of the Industry Day Attendees List**** ****Updated 6 FEB 2020, Posted Releasable Industry Day Slides, Industry Day Attendees List, DRAFT Version of Umbrella SOW, DRAFT Version of Task Order 1 Work Description, and Updated Tech Read Library Instructions**** ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. It is anticipated that Foreign Allied Participation will be excluded at the prime contractor level. A technical library relating to the subject area of this acquisition will be made available. Potential Offerors will first need to request access through AFRL/RI personnel. Full instructions and contact information are contained within attachment 1 of this posting. For planning purposes, potential Offerors who wish to gain access to the Technical Read Library will be required to sign a �Statement of Terms for Receipt of Technical Read Library Access�, provide a copy of an approved DD Form 2345 �Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement�, and provide a letter from the Data Custodian designated on that form authorizing access by whomever will be reviewing the library. Evaluation of the capability packages received in response to the Request for Information (RFI-RIKD-19-01) resulted in a determination that a small business set-aside could be established. A Draft Request for Proposal (RFP) for this effort is anticipated to be released during the 1st quarter of CY 2020. Potential Offerors will be encouraged to review and comment on the Draft RFP, including the Statement of Work (SOW) and Sections L and M. Please monitor this notice for updates. THE ENTIRE SOLICITATION WILL BE ISSUED ON THE BETA SAM WEBSITE AT https://beta.sam.gov/. Paper copies will not be available. The solicitation and any amendments thereto will only be available by downloading the documents from the website. All prospective offerors are responsible for monitoring the site for the release of amendments (if any) or other information pertaining to the solicitation. It is anticipated that the website will provide a registration service that will send an e-mail notification when a change is made to the solicitation. All responsible sources may submit a proposal in response to the RFP which shall be considered. Based on market research, the Government is not using FAR Part 12, Acquisition of Commercial Items, to solicit for the described supplies or services. However, interested parties may identify to the Contracting Officer their interest and capability to satisfy the Government's requirement with a commercial item(s) within thirty (30) days of this notice. Technical questions should be directed to the Contracting Officer's Technical Representative (COTR), Donna Toole at (315) 330-3972, donna.toole.1@us.af.mil. Any contractual questions or questions concerning this Presolicitation Notice should be communicated directly to the Contract Specialist, Matthew Zawisza at (315) 330-4922, matthew.zawisza@us.af.mil, or the Contracting Officer, Terrence Lipinski at (315) 330-4510, terrence.lipinski@us.af.mil. In accordance with AFFARS 5301.91, an Ombudsman has been appointed to hear and facilitate the resolution of concerns from offerors, potential offerors, and others for this acquisition. Before consulting with an Ombudsman, interested parties must first address their concerns, issues, disagreements, and/or recommendations to the Contracting Officer, Terrence Lipinski at (315) 330-4510, terrence.lipinski@us.af.mil, for resolution. AFFARS clause 5352.201-9101, Ombudsman, will be incorporated into the resultant contract. When requested, the Ombudsman will maintain strict confidentiality as to the source of the concern. The existence of the Ombudsman does not affect the authority of the Program Manager, Contracting Officer, or source selection official. Further, the Ombudsman does not participate in the evaluation of proposals, the source selection process, or the adjudication of protests or formal contract disputes. The Ombudsman may refer the party to another official who can resolve the concern. Consulting an Ombudsman does not alter or postpone the timelines for any other processes (e.g., agency level bid protests, GAO bid protests, requests for debriefings, employee-employer actions, contests of OMB Circular A-76 competition performance decisions). If resolution cannot be made by the Contracting Officer, concerned parties may contact the following AFRL Ombudsman: Mr. Steven L. Ewers, 1864 Fourth Street, Wright-Patterson AFB OH 45433-7130, COMM (937) 904-4407, email: steven.ewers@us.af.mil. Concerns, issues, disagreements, and recommendations that cannot be resolved at the AFRL level may be brought by the concerned party for further consideration to the Air Force Ombudsman, Associate Deputy

title: Base Operation Support (BOS) Services for Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Laurel Bay (LB), Laurel Bay Schools, Beaufort, South Carolina, and Townsend Bombing Range Shellman Bluff, Georgia
description: This is not a request for either a quote or proposal, or invitation for bid. The intent of this pre-solicitation synopsis is to notify potential offerors of Base Operation Support (BOS), Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ), Performance-Based contract with Recurring and Non-Recurring services to provide Facility Investment, Pest Control, Electrical and Base Support Vehicle and Equipment (BSVE) services for Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Laurel Bay (LB), Laurel Bay Schools, Beaufort, South Carolina, Townsend Bombing Range Shellman Bluff, Georgia, and outlying areas supported by the installations. The Contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, material and equipment facilities, transportation, incidental engineering, and other items necessary to provide BOS services. Locations include but are not limited to: Marine Corps Air Station (MCAS) Laurel Bay (LB), Laurel Bay Schools, Beaufort, South Carolina, Townsend Bombing Range Shellman Bluff, Georgia, and outlying areas supported by the installations. General Work Requirements: Sub-Annex 1502000 Facility Investment The intent of Facility Investment is to specify the requirements for Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) sub-functions only. The Facility Investment requirements within this sub-annex primarily consist of infrastructure sustainment and minimal restoration and modernization work. Sustainment is the maintenance and repair necessary to keep an inventory of facilities and other assets in good working order. Restoration and modernization normally consists of major rehabilitation and capital improvements that is accomplished through other USMC programs. Some major repair, minor construction and stand-alone demolition may be accomplished as part of Facility Investment. The Contractor shall perform maintenance, repair, alteration, demolition and minor construction for the following: Building and Structures � to include interior and exterior finishes, plumbing (includes backflow prevention devices), grease traps, roofing, foundation, structural components, cathodic protection systems, tanks, POL system, pipelines, relamping, converters, Building Systems -HVAC, Direct Digital Control (DDC), Emergency Management Control System (EMCS), Vertical Transportation Equipment (VTE), intrusion detection systems, bridge and jib cranes, boilers, Unfired Pressure Vessels (UPV), compressed air systems, potable water (including backflow prevention devices), wastewater, and electrical. Sub-Annex 1503020 Pest Control The contractor shall provide pest control services to prevent and control nuisance, structural, turf and ornamental, and medical arthropod and vertebrate pests, including but not limited to cockroaches, termites, ants, fleas, bed bugs, silverfish, stored product pests, mosquitoes, mice, rats, bats, feral dogs and cats and other vertebrates, bees, wasps, pigeons, and nuisance birds. Sub-Annex 1602000 Electrical The Contractor shall provide all labor, management, supervision, tools, material, and equipment to continuously operate, maintain, and repair the electrical power generation plant, transmission systems and distribution systems. The intent is to specify the requirements for electrical power generation, power transmission and distribution. All sources for generating electrical power for utilities, e.g., boilers, wind, solar, gas, etc. Annex 1700000 Base Support Vehicle and Equipment The intent of BSVE is to specify the requirements for a transportation program consisting of vehicles, equipment maintenance and repairs. The vehicle and equipment operations shall include dispatch, Weight Handling Equipment (WHE) / Material Handling Equipment (MHE), Ordinance Handling Equipment (OHE), liquid movements, people movements, operator licensing and training, inspection and certification, and specified administrative program management. Source Selection procedures will be used to select the best value offeror using tradeoff analysis in accordance with FAR Part 15 � Contracting by Negotiation. The solicitation and resulting contract award will be a performance-based service acquisition made to the responsible offeror whose proposal, conforming to the Request for Proposal (RFP), will be advantageous to the Government price and other evaluation factors considered. The offeror�s proposal shall contain a response to each of the evaluation factors and shall be in the form prescribed by the solicitation. The solicitation requires the evaluation of price and the following non-price factors: Factor 1 � Management Approach, Factor 2 � Corporate Experience, Factor 3 � Safety, and Factor 4 � Past Performance. description: ****Updated 13 FEB 2020, Posted an Updated version of the Industry Day Attendees List**** ****Updated 6 FEB 2020, Posted Releasable Industry Day Slides, Industry Day Attendees List, DRAFT Version of Umbrella SOW, DRAFT Version of Task Order 1 Work Description, and Updated Tech Read Library Instructions**** ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE/PROPOSAL: The National Park Service intends to solicit a quote and enter into a contract with Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc located at 1550 Industrial PKWY, Brunswick, Ohio 44212-2349, United States. This requirement is for the repair of the rotary manifold for a John Deere 85G Excavator which requires removal, inspection and reconditioning for Cuyahoga Valley National Park. Murphy Tractor is the only John Deere Certified Dealer that is close to the park in Cleveland/ Akron and the surrounding areas. The rotary manifold assembly (10-port configuration) and associated seal kits are proprietary components designed to OEM specifications. Compatibility, warranty protection, and operational integrity necessitate procurement of John Deere-approved parts and qualified service support. Substituting non-OEM components may compromise system performance, increase failure risk, and create liability exposure. If the park outsourced this requirement to another Certified John Deere Dealer that is further away this would add excessive additional cost for reassembly of the machine and due to transportation costs. Additionally, this equipment must be urgently repaired in order to support park operations for the maintenance of park railroad tracks which could be impeded due to mudslide or other hazards. Failure to repair this equipment in a timely manner could endanger park staff and guests. Due to the above, sole-sourcing to Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc ensures the most expedient and compliant resolution to these urgent repairs. Questions may be directed to Ryan R Begany in writing by email to ryan_begany@ios.doi.gov. NO PHONE inquiries will be accepted.

title: GEC MD8060 Automated Scale Presses Industry Day
description: Special Notice Title of Event: GEC MD8060 Automated Scale Presses Industry Day Audience: Industry Representatives When: 7 April 2026, 0800-1600 Where: Air Force Metrology & Calibration (AFMETCAL) and the Air Force Primary Standards Laboratory (AFPSL), 813 Irving-Wick Dr. W., Heath, OH 43056 Abstract: The Air Force Metrology and Calibration Program (AFMETCAL) is hosting an Industry Day to provide information and gather feedback regarding the potential modification of the GEC MD8060 Automated Scale Presses. This event is critical for potential offerors to gain a comprehensive understanding of the current system and the specific requirements for its modification. The potential modification of the MD8060 would include removing the current hydraulic and electronic systems then installing a manually controlled hydraulic pump that maintains the MD8060�s accuracy of �0.025% rdg and range from 200 to 60,000 lbf. The primary objective of this Industry Day is to allow industry partners the opportunity to inspect the MD8060 firsthand at Air Force Primary Standards Lab (AFPSL). This on-site inspection is essential for understanding the requirement and developing an informed and effective solution. We encourage industry to identify potential risks and propose mitigation strategies related to the system modification. Potential offerors on any future solicitation are required to inspect the MD8060 on site, as they likely would not be able to submit a competitive proposal without a site visit. In no event shall failure to inspect the MD8060 on site constitute grounds for a claim after any resulting contract award. Objectives: Provide early engagement and communication to Industry Provide a forum to discuss modification strategies Improve the quality of any future solicitation Identify vendors interested and capable of executing modification of the MD8060 Who Should Attend? Both large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this Industry Day event. For this Industry Day, the Government will permit a maximum of three (3) individuals per vendor to register and attend. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code to be used for this procurement is 334516 (Laboratory Analytical Instruments Manufacturing). Items for Discussion: To facilitate effective exchange, the Government requests questions in writing prior to the Industry Day. This will allow the Government to conduct research in advance of scheduled one-on-one sessions and come prepared to answer your questions. Please submit your specific questions to BOTH frank.capuano@us.af.mil and thomas.carson.2@us.af.mil. Answers may be limited as the Government is in the Market Research phase. The Government is not requesting capability statements or briefings at this time. Scheduled one-on-one sessions will allow interested vendors the opportunity to openly communicate with the Government by providing comments and inputs for consideration during the development of the solicitation. Times for the one-on-one sessions will be scheduled and communicated with registered attendees prior to the Industry Day. Sessions will be no more than 60 minutes and discussion will focus on the MD8060 requirements. In the event an interested party cannot attend on the scheduled date, an alternate date for a site visit will be accommodated as necessary to ensure maximum participation. To ensure transparency, non-proprietary questions and answers will be recorded, sanitized, and placed on SAM.gov. Please e-mail proposed topics and questions that you may have no later than 27 March 2026. Registration: Pre-registration is MANDATORY for attendance. Please submit the following information electronically to BOTH frank.capuano@us.af.mil and thomas.carson.2@us.af.mil no later than 2:00 PM EDT 27 March 2026 to pre-register. Information addressing security, directions, and individual session times will be provided to respondents. For this Industry Day, the Government will permit a maximum of three (3) individuals per vendor to register and attend. Only group registrations will be processed. The following information shall be provided for each attendee: 1. Individual attendees' full name and title 2. Individual attendees' e-mail address 3. Company name 4. Company Cage Code 5. Small Business Status 6. Telephone number 7. Visitor request form (To be provided upon notice of pre-registration) 7. Do you wish to have your company name included on a published list of attendees? Additional Information: Any submitted information may be used to structure future solicitations. Sensitive, proprietary, or otherwise confidential information must be marked appropriately in the response. Information received from respondents will not be shared with other vendors. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the market research. Additionally, information gathered through this meeting may influence RFQ development. This notification does not constitute an Invitation for Bids (IFB), a Request for Quote (RFQ), or a Request for Proposal (RFP) and it should not be construed as a commitment of any kind by the Government to issue a formal solicitation, award a contract, or conduct an acquisition in any particular way. The U.S. Government is in no way liable to pay for or reimburse any companies or entities that respond to this announcement. Any costs incurred by interested companies in response to this announcement or incurred for participation in the Industry Day will NOT be reimbursed. All information marked as proprietary information will be safeguarded to prevent disclosure to non-Government personnel and entities. The acquisition strategy for the modification of the GEC MD8060 Automated Scale Presses has not been finalized; this requirement is in the market research and planning phase. No solicitation or projected solicitation date is available at this time. Points of Contact: All communication regarding this solicitation should be sent to BOTH of the following individuals: Thomas Carson, Contracting Officer thomas.carson.2@us.af.mil 937-713-5844 Frank Capuano, Contract Specialist frank.capuano@us.af.mil 937-713-5842

These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. title: J--Excavator Repair - CUVA
description: THIS IS A NOTICE OF AWARD FOR A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT AND NOT A REQUEST FOR QUOTE: The National Park Service is awarding Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc located at 1550 Industrial PKWY, Brunswick, Ohio 44212-2349, United States; a large business, the contract to provide the Excavator Repairs service requirement for Cuyahoga Valley National Park, which is being purchased for $15,826.74. Please see attached justification document for more details. This requirement is for the repair of the rotary manifold for a John Deere 85G Excavator which requires removal, inspection and reconditioning for Cuyahoga Valley National Park. Murphy Tractor is the only John Deere Certified Dealer that is close to the park in Cleveland/ Akron and the surrounding areas. The rotary manifold assembly (10-port configuration) and associated seal kits are proprietary components designed to OEM specifications. Compatibility, warranty protection, and operational integrity necessitate procurement of John Deere-approved parts and qualified service support. Substituting non-OEM components may compromise system performance, increase failure risk, and create liability exposure. If the park outsourced this requirement to another Certified John Deere Dealer that is further away this would add excessive additional cost for reassembly of the machine and due to transportation costs. Additionally, this equipment must be urgently repaired in order to support park operations for the maintenance of park railroad tracks which could be impeded due to mudslide or other hazards. Failure to repair this equipment in a timely manner could endanger park staff and guests. Due to the above, sole-sourcing to Murphy Tractor & Equipment Co, Inc ensures the most expedient and compliant resolution to these urgent repairs. Questions may be directed to Ryan R Begany in writing by email to ryan_begany@ios.doi.gov. NO PHONE inquiries will be accepted.

title: GEOSPATIAL INTELLIGENCE PROCESSING AND EXPLOITATION (GeoPEX)
description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Geospatial Intelligence Processing and Exploitation (GeoPEX) BAA NUMBER: BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 SEP 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 SEP 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY22 � 30 Sep 2021 FY23 � 30 Sep 2022 FY24 � 30 Sep 2023 FY25 � 30 Sep 2024 FY26 � 30 Sep 2025 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the Beta SAM website at https://beta.SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking white papers for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to provide geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) in all its forms and from whatever source - imagery, imagery intelligence, or geospatial data and information - to ensure a solid foundation of knowledge for planning, decision, and action while creating tailored, customer-specific geospatial intelligence, analytic services, and solutions. This BAA is a follow-on to BAA FA8750-17-S-7004 Knowledge Aided GEOINT Latency Reduction (KAGLR) BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 24 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $250K to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. description: Update - Redacted Justification and Approval added to special notice. In accordance with FAR 6.302-1, the Defense Logistics Agency (DLA) anticipates awarding a modification to existing DLA Distribution Contract SP3300-21-D-5002 on a sole source basis to Olgoonik Federal, LLC. This contract provides labor to support workload surges, unforeseen/unplanned workload, contingency operations and special projects. The modification would increase the ceiling amount as the contract has been outpacing the anticipated spend rate. Pursuant to the exception under FAR 6.302-1(a)(2)(iii), only Olgoonik Federal, LLC is capable of providing the services at this time; award to any other source will result in unacceptable delays and would preclude DLA from reacting timely to requirements. The modification to current contract SP3300-21-D-5002 will serve as a temporary solution to fulfill immediate mission requirements. A follow-on procurement is in process. description: ****Updated 6 FEB 2020, Posted Releasable Industry Day Slides, Industry Day Attendees List, DRAFT Version of Umbrella SOW, DRAFT Version of Task Order 1 Work Description, and Updated Tech Read Library Instructions**** ****Updated 3 Dec 2019, Industry Day private appointments limited to only small businesses.**** PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE: The Air Force Research Laboratory, Information Directorate, Rome NY (AFRL/RI) has a requirement provide a focused yet flexible, rapid, agile contracting vehicle between Air Force Research Laboratory, its Products Centers, and the Operational Community to support rapid research, development, prototyping, demonstration, evaluation, and transition of Counter small Unmanned Aircraft System (C-sUAS) capabilities. These capabilities are to be used in combating Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS)�and others leveraging COTS technology�presently being used by our adversaries in asymmetric warfare against U.S. military personnel and materiel. Emphasis will be placed on: a) development of technology capability solutions that address specific user requirements; b) delivery of prototype technologies for evaluation and feedback in the context of the user�s operational environment; and c) provision of a mechanism for user acquisition of limited product quantities required for operational introduction of technologies. Anticipated deliverables include software, hardware, technical documentation and technical reports. For the aforementioned requirements, the Government anticipates a single award Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (ID/IQ) research and development (R&D) contract with Cost-Plus-Fixed-Fee Completion (CPFF/C) Task Orders, an ordering period of seventy-two (72) months, and a maximum ordering amount of approximately $490,000,000. The North American Industry Classification Systems (NAICS) code for this effort is 541715 with a small business size standard of 1,500 employees based on the Aircraft, Aircraft Engine, and Engine Parts exception. At time of award, the successful Offeror must be able to provide approximately 20% of proposed personnel to be TS/SCI cleared and assigned at time of award, with graduated increases in proportion over time. During performance, the Contractor's continued ability to meet security requirements will be evaluated. It is anticipated that Foreign Allied Participation will be excluded at the prime contractor level. A technical library relating to the subject area of this acquisition will be made available. Potential Offerors will first need to request access through AFRL/RI personnel. Full instructions and contact information are contained within attachment 1 of this posting. For planning purposes, potential Offerors who wish to gain access to the Technical Read Library will be required to sign a �Statement of Terms for Receipt of Technical Read Library Access�, provide a copy of an approved DD Form 2345 �Militarily Critical Technical Data Agreement�, and provide a letter from the Data Custodian designated on that form authorizing access by whomever will be reviewing the library. description: NAICS CODE: 541715 FEDERAL AGENCY NAME: Department of the Air Force, Air Force Materiel Command, AFRL - Rome Research Site, AFRL/Information Directorate, 26 Electronic Parkway, Rome, NY, 13441-4514 BAA ANNOUNCEMENT TYPE: Initial announcement BROAD AGENCY ANNOUNCEMENT (BAA) TITLE: Geospatial Intelligence Processing and Exploitation (GeoPEX) BAA NUMBER: BAA FA8750-21-S-7006 PART I � OVERVIEW INFORMATION This announcement is for an Open, 2 Step BAA which is open and effective until 30 SEP 2026. Only white papers will be accepted as initial submissions; formal proposals will be accepted by invitation only. While white papers will be considered if received prior to 3 PM Eastern Standard Time (EST) on 30 SEP 2026, the following submission dates are suggested to best align with projected funding: FY22 � 30 Sep 2021 FY23 � 30 Sep 2022 FY24 � 30 Sep 2023 FY25 � 30 Sep 2024 FY26 � 30 Sep 2025 Offerors should monitor the Contract Opportunities on the Beta SAM website at https://beta.SAM.gov in the event this announcement is amended. CONCISE SUMMARY OF TECHNOLOGY REQUIREMENT: Seeking white papers for research, development, integration, test and evaluation of technologies/techniques to provide geospatial intelligence (GEOINT) in all its forms and from whatever source - imagery, imagery intelligence, or geospatial data and information - to ensure a solid foundation of knowledge for planning, decision, and action while creating tailored, customer-specific geospatial intelligence, analytic services, and solutions. This BAA is a follow-on to BAA FA8750-17-S-7004 Knowledge Aided GEOINT Latency Reduction (KAGLR) BAA ESTIMATED FUNDING: Total funding for this BAA is approximately $99.9M. Individual awards will not normally exceed 24 months with dollar amounts normally ranging from $250K to $10M. There is also the potential to make awards up to any dollar value as long as the value does not exceed the available BAA ceiling amount. ANTICIPATED INDIVIDUAL AWARDS: Multiple Awards are anticipated. TYPE OF INSTRUMENTS THAT MAY BE AWARDED: Procurement contracts, grants, cooperative agreements or other transactions (OT) depending upon the nature of the work proposed. In the event that an Other Transaction for Prototype agreement is awarded as a result of this competitive BAA, and the prototype project is successfully completed, there is the potential for a prototype project to transition to award of a follow-on production contract or transaction. The Other Transaction for Prototype agreement itself will also contain a similar notice of a potential follow-on production contract or agreement. AGENCY CONTACT INFORMATION: All white paper submissions and any questions of a technical nature shall be directed to the cognizant Technical Point of Contact (TPOC) as specified below (unless otherwise specified in the technical area): BAA PROGRAM MANAGER: Bernard J. Clarke AFRL/RIGD 525 Brooks Rd Rome, NY 13441-4505 Telephone: (315)330-2106 Email: Bernard.Clarke@us.af.mil Questions of a contractual/business nature shall be directed to the cognizant contracting officer, as specified below: Amber Buckley Email: Amber.Buckley@us.af.mil Emails must reference the solicitation (BAA) number and title of the acquisition. Pre-Proposal Communication between Prospective Offerors and Government Representatives: Dialogue between prospective offerors and Government representatives is encouraged. Technical and contracting questions can be resolved in writing or through open discussions. Discussions with any of the points of contact shall not constitute a commitment by the Government to subsequently fund or award any proposed effort. Only Contracting Officers are legally authorized to commit the Government. Offerors are cautioned that evaluation ratings may be lowered and/or proposal rejected if proposal preparation (Proposal format, content, etc.) and/or submittal instructions are not followed. description: PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE W912HV26BA007 FY26 MCN P309, School Age Care Centers Replacement Camp Foster and McTureous, Okinawa, Japan The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Japan District (POJ) is providing a PRE-SOLICITATION notice pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) 5.101(a) (https://www.acquisition.gov/far-overhaul) for an upcoming Invitation for Bid (IFB). PROJECT INFORMATION Project Title: FY26 MCN P309, School Age Care Centers Replacement Project Location: Camp Foster and McTureous, Okinawa, Japan Product Service Code (PSC): Y1AZ - CONSTRUCTION OF OTHER ADMINISTRATIVE FACILITIES AND SERVICE BUILDINGS NAICS Code: 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction Project Magnitude: Between $25,000,000 and $50,000,000 (Between �3,479,087,500 and �7,522,075,000) Project(s) Description: Construct low-rise reinforced concrete structures to replace the current School Age Care Centers (SACC) located on Camp Foster (Building 1) and Camp McTureous (Building 2). The functional areas will include spaces for the lobby, reception, activity rooms, a large kitchen, restrooms, a multi-purpose half-court room without bleachers, a janitor room, administrative offices, a STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics)/computer room, and storage rooms. Exterior requirements will include benches, fencing, and a children's drop-off/pick-up waiting area. Construct an outdoor playground area next to SAC at each site. It should include energy-absorbing poured flooring and age-appropriate playground equipment. Facility-related control systems include cybersecurity features following current Department of Defense (DoD) criteria. title: Automated Background Investigation System (ABIS) Maintenance and Support
description: The CFPB, PSO, requires continued contractor support for the operation, maintenance and enhancement of the Automated Background Investigation System (ABIS). ABIS serves as an established personnel security system supporting the administrative processing, tracking, management and transmission of personnel security and investigative information in support of background investigation and personnel vetting activities. The objective of this requirement is to ensure the continued availability, reliability, security and functionality of ABIS while enabling the system to adapt to evolving CFPB operational needs and Government wide personnel vetting policies, standards, technologies and external systems. Contractor support shall include ongoing system maintenance and technical support; configuration and software updates; maintenance of existing interfaces and data exchanges; and the development and implementation of approved enhancements and modifications necessary to support CFPB business requirements and maintain compatibility with changes to CFPB and external Federal systems, processes and requirements. The contractor shall also support ABIS modernization and adaptation activities necessary to address evolving Federal personnel vetting initiatives and requirements, including Trusted Workforce 2.0 and changes, services, policies or requirements established by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM), Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), Performance Accountability Council Program Management Office (PAC PMO) and other applicable Federal entities.

description: Le marché a pour objet la réalisation de la mission de Maitrise d’œuvre pour la restauration des façades et des menuiseries extérieures situées avenue Victoria et rue Adolphe Adam ainsi que des façades sur cours intérieures du bâtiment sis 12-14 quai des Gesvres à Paris (75004). Il y a quatre façades extérieures principales et quatre petites façades aux angles chanfreinés. Les travaux portent sur la restauration des façades en pierre de taille et en enduit, des ferronneries, du système d’évacuation des eaux pluviales, des éléments en plomb et le remplacement des menuiseries extérieures. L’immeuble datant des années 1860, des compétences en restauration patrimoniales seront nécessaires à la maîtrise d’œuvre pour mener à bien cette mission et dialoguer avec les services des Bâtiments de France. Les travaux concernés sont soumis à une autorisation administrative qui devra être réalisée par le titulaire du présent marché. Enfin, le site hébergeant des services de police actifs 24/24 et 7/7, et du public, la planification en amont de l’organisation du chantier en site occupé sensible est obligatoirement à prendre en compte dès les phases Études. A titre d’information, une première opération de restauration des façades quai de Gesvres et rue Saint-Martin sera lancée en travaux en 2027 et ne fait pas partie de cette mission. Le titulaire du marché se verra confier les missions de base suivantes : Études d’avant-projet sommaire (APS) ; Études d’avant-projet définitif (APD) ; Études de projet (PRO) ; Assistance pour la passation des contrats de travaux (ACT/DCE) ; Examen de conformité - visa (VISA) ; Direction de l'exécution du contrat de travaux (DET) ; Assistance lors des opérations de réception et pendant la période de garantie de parfait achèvement (AOR). Le contenu des éléments de mission est fixé au Code de la commande publique et à l’arrêté du 22 mars 2019 précisant les modalités techniques d'exécution des éléments de mission de maîtrise d'œuvre confiés par des maîtres d'ouvrage publics à des prestataires de droit privé.

title: Germany – Cardiology services – AOK-Priomed Ambulante Eingriffe am Herzen Vertrag gemäß § 140a SGB V
description: Gegenstand dieser Veröffentlichung ist der Vertrag zur Besonderen Versorgung "AOK-Priomed Ambulante Eingriffe am Herzen gemäß § 140a SGB V" mit niedergelassenen Kardiologen bzw. Herzchirurgen, um herzchirurgische Leistungen effizienter und zum Vorteil der Patienten zu erbringen, im Rahmen eines sogenannten "Open-House-Modells". Unter Vorgabe einheitlicher Vertragskonditionen sowie eines einheitlichen Zugangsverfahrens wird allen geeigneten und interessierten im Bereich der KV Hessen niedergelassenen Fachärzte für Innere Medizin/ Schwerpunkt Kardiologie oder Fachärzte für Herzchirurgie und Einrichtungen, welche die geforderten Strukturvoraussetzungen persönlich oder durch angestellte Ärzte erfüllen, der Beitritt zum Vertrag angeboten. Interessierte Ärzte können dazu unter der Kontaktadresse die Vertrags- und Teilnahmeunterlagen reinhold.preiss@kardiologen-hessen.de anfordern. Voraussetzung für den Abschluss eines Vertrages ist, dass der interessierte Arzt die angeforderten Teilnahmeunterlagen vollständig ausgefüllt und unterzeichnet vorlegt. Jeder Arzt, der die Teilnahmevoraussetzungen erfüllt, kann dem Vertrag beitreten. Eine Exklusivität ist nicht gegeben. Individuelle Vertragsverhandlungen werden nicht durchgeführt. Der Beitritt zum Vertrag kann jederzeit bis zum 30.09.2026 und zu den gleichen Bedingungen erfolgen. Mit diesem Vertrag sollen ambulante Eingriffe am Herzen durchgeführt werden. Hierunter fallen Neu-Implantationen, Aggregatwechsel, Aggregat- und Sondenwechsel von Herzschrittmachern sowie die Neuimplantationen von Eventrecordern. Die Behandlung der vertraglich aufgeführten Indikationen erfolgt in Form einer indikationsbezogenen herzchirurgischen Versorgung mit der ambulanten Nachsorge. Der Vertrag hat das Ziel einer indikationsgerechten und qualitätsgesicherten Patientenversorgung durch ausführliche Informationen über den Eingriff und die Verkürzung der Wartezeiten vor der geplanten Operation. Er beinhaltet eine verbesserte und abgestimmte diagnostische Behandlung bei Herzerkrankungen, individuelle Aggregate und zum jeweiligen Eingriff eine abgestimmte Nachsorge. Die Wahl der Aggregate bzw. der Einsatz qualitativ hochwertiger Produkte soll die Versorgung hinsichtlich Qualität und Wirtschaftlichkeit verbessern. Der Inhalt des Vertrages zur Besonderen Versorgung steht für alle interessierten Ärzte fest und ist nicht verhandelbar. Bei der vorliegenden Veröffentlichung handelt es sich nicht um die Vergabe eines öffentlichen Auftrags im Sinne der Richtlinie 2014/24/EU bzw. des Vergaberechts. Um ein weitestgehendes Maß an Transparenz für die beabsichtigten Vertragsschlüsse zu gewährleisten, erfolgt die Veröffentlichung im Supplement zum Amtsblatt der Europäischen Union. In Ermangelung eines entsprechenden Veröffentlichungsformulars für Open-House-Verfahren wird die Auftragsbekanntmachung genutzt. Die daraus resultierenden begrifflichen Vorgaben, wie bspw. die Verfahrensbezeichnung "Offenes Verfahren" oder die Angaben "Schlusstermin für den Eingang der Angebote" oder "Bedingungen für die Öffnung der Angebote" sind einzig der Nutzung der eFormsStandards sowie der Veröffentlichungsplattform geschuldet. title: France – Drinking-water distribution – Concession des services publics de l'eau potable et de l'assainissement collectif de Nîmes Métropole
description: Le contrat a pour objet l'exploitation et la gestion des services publics de l'eau potable et de l'assainissement collectif de Nîmes Métropole. Afin de bénéficier de la meilleure économie et d'une uniformité des services rendus aux usagers, la communauté d'agglomération Nîmes Métropole a choisi un contrat unique pour la gestion des services publics de l'eau potable et de l'assainissement collectif. En 2024 le service de l'eau potable dessert 101 876 abonnés pour un volume facturé de 14 955 989 m3 et le service assainissement collectif dessert 91 471 abonnés pour un volume assujetti de 12 499 938 m3. Le démarrage de la gestion des services est prévue au 1er janvier 2028 pour un durée de 10 ans. En cas de signature ou de prise d'effet du contrat postérieure à cette date, la durée de la concession sera réduite en conséquence afin de maintenir la date du terme de la fin de concession au 31 décembre 2037. Nîmes Métropole demandera la création d'une société dédiée aux candidats à la concession.

title: Belgium – Sewage work – Perwez - Extension, mise au tertiaire et rénovation de la station d'épuration de Perwez
description: Le présent marché a pour objet l’EXTENSION, LA MISE AU TERTIAIRE ET LA RENOVATION DE LA STATION D’EPURATION DES EAUX USEES DE PERWEZ. L'entreprise consiste à réaliser les travaux à la fois de génie civil, de démantèlement, d'électromécanique, d’électricité, d’automatisme et de supervision pour l’extension, la mise au tertiaire et la rénovation de la station d'épuration, suivant les documents et les prescriptions du présent cahier spécial des charges. La station doit pouvoir traiter, biologiquement, une pollution d'origine domestique équivalente à 7000 EH, à 180L/EH.j, considérant la DCO à 120 g/EH.j et les MES à 120 g/EH.j. Le process épuratoire retenu pour la ligne de traitement des eaux est la boue activée. Les nouvelles normes de traitement imposées sont reprises dans les clauses techniques du présent cahier des charges. Le présent marché inclut : • La construction d’une nouvelle ligne de traitement des eaux reprenant les 7.000 EH ; • La construction d’une ligne de traitement des boues ; • La construction d’un nouveau bâtiment technique et administratif ; • Le démantèlement de l’ancienne ligne de traitement des eaux, inclus les vieux équipements EM ; • Le démantèlement de l’ancien bâtiment technique et administratif. ; • Les mesures transitoires et équipements temporaires pour maintenir la station en fonctionnement durant les travaux. L'entreprise consiste à réaliser les travaux à la fois de génie civil, de démantèlement, d'électromécanique, d’électricité, d’automatisme et de supervision pour l’extension, la mise au tertiaire et la rénovation de la station d'épuration, suivant les documents et les prescriptions du présent cahier spécial des charges. La station doit pouvoir traiter, biologiquement, une pollution d'origine domestique équivalente à 7000 EH, à 180L/EH.j, considérant la DCO à 120 g/EH.j et les MES à 120 g/EH.j. Le process épuratoire retenu pour la ligne de traitement des eaux est la boue activée. Les nouvelles normes de traitement imposées sont reprises dans les clauses techniques du présent cahier des charges. Le présent marché inclut : • La construction d’une nouvelle ligne de traitement des eaux reprenant les 7.000 EH ; • La construction d’une ligne de traitement des boues ; • La construction d’un nouveau bâtiment technique et administratif ; • Le démantèlement de l’ancienne ligne de traitement des eaux, inclus les vieux équipements EM ; • Le démantèlement de l’ancien bâtiment technique et administratif. ; • Les mesures transitoires et équipements temporaires pour maintenir la station en fonctionnement durant les travaux. Le présent dossier porte sur le mode de réalisation général de l’installation, étant entendu que les études techniques du matériel ainsi que les études de stabilité seront à fournir par le soumissionnaire. Les plans et documents à fournir sont définis dans les clauses. Les volumes et conditions dimensionnelles étant prescrites par le cahier spécial des charges, le soumissionnaire s’engage par sa mise en œuvre du processus au sens général (construction, ligne d’eau, automatisation, réglage) à garantir la performance requise pour le traitement.

Les prestations comprennent notamment : - l'élaboration des menus adaptés aux différentes catégories de convives ; - la confection des repas dans le respect des recommandations nutritionnelles et de la règlementation applicable à la restauration collective ; - la fourniture de repas répondant aux besoins spécifiques des jeunes enfants, notamment en matière de textures, de grammages et d'équilibre alimentaire ; - la prise en compte des régimes alimentaires particuliers, des allergies et des protocoles d'accueil individualisés (PAI) transmis par la collectivité ; - le conditionnement, l'étiquetage et la traçabilité des denrées ; - la livraison des repas sur les différents sites de la collectivité dans le respect de la chaine du froid ; - la transmission des informations relatives à la composition des repas, aux allergènes et à l'origine des produits conformément à la règlementation en vigueur. Le titulaire s'engage à fournir des repas variés, équilibrés et de qualité, adaptés à l'âge des convives et élaborés dans le respect des exigences sanitaires, nutritionnelles et environnementales applicables à la restauration collective. title: Netherlands – Agricultural services – Landbouwbedrijf

De organisatie waarin deze activiteiten plaatsvinden wordt net landbouwbedrijf genoemd In de huidige vorm is het landbouwbedrijf een unieke beheer eenheid waarmee de gemeente Tilburg ondersteund en ontzorgd wordt in het beheer van haar landbouwgronden

Rozpoczęcie realizacji Inwestycji planowane jest na III/IV kwartał 2026 r. 5. Szczegółowy opis przedmiotu zamówienia został zawarty w Załączniku nr 1 do SWZ. Zabezpieczenie musi być wniesione w pełnej wysokości, niezależnie od formy jego wniesienia, najpóźniej w dniu zawarcia umowy, ale przed jej podpisaniem. title: Germany – Research and development services and related consultancy services – Bereitstellung einer fachgerechten Bewertung von gegrindeten Oberflächentexturen auf Betonfahrbahnen in der ZEB - Berührungslose Ermittlung der Längsebenheit
description: Die Bewertung der Längsebenheit erfordert seit Einführung der Technischen Prüfvorschriften für die berührungslose Messung von Fahrbahnoberflächen [1,2] die Bestimmung des wahren Höhenlängsprofils. Zur Messung des wahren Höhenlängsprofils eignet sich bisher nur das High-Speed Monitoring – Verfahren (HRM). Vergleichbare, z. B. in anderen Ländern verwendete Verfahren, wie ein Inertial-Profilometer, (Abstandsmessung in Kombination mit einem Beschleunigungssensor) sind zurzeit nicht zulassungsfähig. Für abweichende Oberflächenstrukturen wie beispielsweise Grindingstrukturen ist das HRM-Verfahren in seiner aktuellen Form jedoch nicht geeignet. Aufgrund des Materialabtrags entsteht auf gegrindeten Oberflächen ein längs gerichtetes, alternierendes Steg-Rille-Muster, wodurch geringe örtliche Abweichungen der mehrfachabgetasteten Punkte zu großen Abweichungen in den relativen Höhenmessungen der Lasersensoren führen können. Zusätzlich führen schon geringe Winkel zwischen den längs gerichteten Strukturen und der Fahrtrichtung des Messfahrzeuges zu einer Aufprägung einer künstlichen Unebenheit. Die Genauigkeit von Messsystemen, welche auf Basis der berührungslosen Messung arbeiten, können daher von den Grindingstrukturen stark negativ beeinflusst werden. Das Ziel dieses Vorhabens ist die Identifizierung bzw. Entwicklung und Erprobung eines Messverfahrens, dass die berührungslose Messung gegrindeter Strukturen ermöglicht. Dazu sollen die Auswirkungen der gerichteten Strukturen von Grindingtexturen auf die gängigen Messverfahren zur Ermittlung von Höhenlängsprofilen, wie dem HRM-Balken beschrieben und mit speziellen, für Grindingtexturen angepassten Varianten dieser Systeme bzw. alternativer Messsysteme verglichen werden. Die Grundlage dieses Vergleiches sollen Messungen mit dem Planografen bilden, da dieser aufgrund der Breite seines Messrades nicht bzw. weniger anfällig für die Einflüsse einer gegrindeten Textur ist. Außerdem soll neben der Entwicklung eines berührungslosen, schnellfahrenden Messverfahrens ein nachvollziehbar begründetes Konzept zur Berechnung der Höhenlängsprofilpunkte, unter Berücksichtigung von Steg und Rille der Grindingtexturen, erarbeitet werden. Ein derartiges Messverfahren wäre idealerweise sowohl in der Zustandserfassung, als auch bei bauvertraglichen Messungen verwendbar und sollte auf allen heute bekannten Straßenoberflächen funktionieren.

title: France – Miscellaneous special-purpose machinery – Acquisition d'un système de plasma atmosphérique
description: Le système sera utilisé pour réaliser des expériences de condensation et de nucléation de divers matériaux introduits dans le plasma sous forme de poudres. A noter que l’introduction d’éléments chimiques au sein du plasma sous forme d’espèces dissoutes dans le solvant sera également une option technique. Les poudres seront rapidement vaporisées dans le plasma puis condensées au fur et à mesure que la vapeur sera éloignée du plasma. Au cours de ce transport, le refroidissement permet une nucléation et une condensation homogènes de particules de taille nanométrique qui peuvent être collectées directement à partir de la vapeur le long d'un gradient thermique, sans aucune interaction préalable avec le boîtier. Au-dessous du plasma se trouvera une chambre utilisée pour la collecte des particules nucléées dans la vapeur dérivée du refroidissement du plasma. La nucléation aura lieu sans interaction avec les parois internes de la chambre. Il sera possible de collecter des particules générées à différentes températures au sein de la chambre.

description: Gegenstand dieser Veröffentlichung ist der Abschluss nicht exklusiver Rabattvereinbarungen nach § 130a Abs. 8 SGB V über Arzneimittel mit dem Wirkstoff Eltrombopag (ATC-Code nach WHO: B02BX05 unter Ausschluss der Indikation - erworbene schwere aplastische Anämie -, es sei denn, der pharmazeutische Unternehmer ist hierfür Inhaber geltender Patentrechte oder durch eine patentwahrende Lizenz zum Vertrieb berechtigt). Der Vertragsabschluss erfolgt im Rahmen eines sog. Open-House-Modells, d. h. ein Vertragsabschluss steht innerhalb des Teilnahmezeitraums allen interessierten pharmazeutischen Unternehmen offen, sofern diese die Teilnahmevoraussetzungen erfüllen und akzeptieren. Dies hat zur Folge, dass individuelle Vertragsverhandlungen nicht geführt werden und eine (Liefer-)Exklusivität nicht gegeben ist. Es wird darauf hingewiesen, dass die Abnahmemenge unbekannt ist, da diese von der Nachfrage und der Entwicklung der Versichertenzahl, von dem Verordnungsverhalten der Ärzte sowie dem Abgabe- und Bevorratungsverhalten der öffentlichen Apotheken abhängig ist. Mindestabnahmemengen werden demensprechend nicht garantiert. Interessierte pharmazeutische Unternehmer können die Teilnahmeunterlagen über den Projektraum des Deutschen Vergabeportals (DTVP) herunterladen. Dazu ist zunächst ein Antrag auf Zugang zum Projektraum erforderlich. Nach erfolgter Freischaltung durch die Auftraggeberin kann anschließend auf die Teilnahmeunterlagen zugegriffen werden. Über den Inhalt der Teilnahmeunterlagen - insbesondere über den Inhalt der Rabattvereinbarung und den dort genannten Rabatten - ist absolutes Stillschweigen zu bewahren. Eine vollständige oder teilweise Weitergabe oder Zugänglichmachung von Inhalten der Teilnahmeunterlagen an bzw. für Dritte bedarf der vorherigen schriftlichen Zustimmung der Auftraggeberin. Sofern von einer Teilnahme abgesehen wird, sind alle Unterlagen unverzüglich datenschutzgerecht zu vernichten. Die einzureichenden Unterlagen ergeben sich aus den im Projektraum hinterlegten Dokumenten "Anschreiben" und "Erläuterungen der Vertragsbedingungen". Die Kommunikation, einschließlich der Übermittlung der Teilnahmeunterlagen, erfolgt elektronisch über das Vergabeportal DTVP; Einzelheiten hierzu sind den zuvor genannten Dokumenten zu entnehmen. Etwaige anderslautende Angaben in der Auftragsbekanntmachung sind technischen Gründen geschuldet und beanspruchen keine Verbindlichkeit. Teilnahmeanträge können erstmals bis zum 04.09.2025 eingereicht werden. Alle weiteren Einreichungsfristen entnehmen Sie bitte der im Projektraum hinterlegten Anlage "Einreichungsfristen". Fällt der Tag der Einreichungsfrist auf einen Sonnabend, Sonntag oder bundesweit gesetzlichen Feiertag, so tritt an die Stelle eines solchen Tages der nächste Werktag. Bei verspätetem Zugang werden die eingereichten Teilnahmeanträge zur nächsten Einreichungsfrist berücksichtigt. Die Rabattvereinbarung endet, unabhängig vom Datum des Vertragsschlusses, spätestens zum 30.09.2026. Die Auftraggeberin behält sich vor, das Open-House-Verfahren vorzeitig zu beenden, insbesondere im Falle des Abschlusses exklusiver Rabattvereinbarungen; in diesem Fall enden die bereits geschlossenen Rabattvereinbarungen nach Maßgabe der vertraglichen Bestimmungen. Den Erfahrungen der Auftraggeberin nach treten exklusive Rabattvereinbarungen in der Regel 8 bis 12 Monate nach der Veröffentlichung der entsprechenden Auftragsbekanntmachung im Supplement zum Amtsblatt der Europäischen Union in Kraft.

La consultation porte sur des prestations de maintenance et de travaux de télésurveillance et télé-interpellation des immeubles administratifs, ainsi que de vidéosurveillance des immeubles collectifs de PARTENORD LE GROUPE et PARTENIUM. Les prestations sont réparties en 2 lots thématiques. Chaque lot fera l'objet d'un accord-cadre à bons de commande mono-attributaire conclu avec un montant minimum et avec un montant maximum annuel mentionnés dans la rubrique description des lots, montants identiques en cas de reconduction de la période. En application de l'article L.2112-2 du Code de la Commande Publique, les lots comportent une action d'insertion sociale par l'activité économique

description: Lieu d'exécution : Résidence Cartault à PUTEAUX composée de 3 bâtiments : 4, rue Cartault, 4 bis rue Cartault, 6, rue Cartault - Travaux sur CARTAULT 1 soit le 4, rue Cartault (Tranche Ferme et Tranches Optionnelles), - Travaux sur CARTAULT 2 soit les 4 bis et 6, rue Cartault (PSE). Les travaux objet du présent marché sont donc traités en Entreprise Générale (EG) en un lot unique (1 seul et unique marché de travaux) avec un programme de travaux décomposés en macros-lots : - Lot n° 0 - Organisation du chantier - Lot n° 1 - Demolition - gros-oeuvre - doublages - plâtrerie - carrelage - faïence - aménagements extérieurs - Lot n° 2 - Façades - Lot n° 3 - Couverture - étanchéité - Lot n° 4 - Serrurerie - métallerie - Lot n° 5 - Menuiseries extérieures - Lot n° 6 - Menuiseries intérieures - Lot n° 7 - Peinture - Lot n° 8 - Revêtements de sols - Lot n° 9 - Plomberie - ventilation - chauffage - Lot n° 10 - Electricité - Lot n°11 - Ventilation Les travaux propres à chaque « corps d'état » sont détaillés aux Cahier des Clauses Techniques Particulières (CCTP). Il est bien précisé qu'il s'agit d'un lot unique composé de macro-lots (et non de lots en corps d'état séparés). La dénomination de « lot » mentionnée dans les pièces techniques doit être interprétée comme équivalente à « macro-lot »
